react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP ORA identified the Sulfatase and aromatase pathway (WP:WP5368, FDR 7.99e-16) and Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, FDR 6.44e-15) as the top multi-DB hits, with five C19/C18 steroids (dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, testosterone, estrone, 17β-estradiol) hitting both pathways. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovered the same biological module as its top-ranked hit (p=8.40e-05), achieving a perfect 11/11 metabolite overlap on the androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism network node. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis, p=8.39e-06) as the single significant hit, with the same five steroids as the RaMP result. The six resolved driver metabolites occupy sequential positions in the steroidogenic cascade: dehydroepiandrosterone and androstenedione sit upstream of testosterone, which feeds into estrone and 17β-estradiol. CYP19A1 (aromatase) mediates the critical androstenedione-to-estrone conversion bridging androgen and estrogen arms. The remaining two metabolites — menadione (vitamin K3, KEGG:C05377) and indoleacetaldehyde (tryptophan–indole axis, KEGG:C00637) — did not reach significance in any paradigm and are excluded as peripheral signals.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on androgen and estrogen metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA identified the Sulfatase and aromatase pathway (WP:WP5368) as the top hit with FDR=7.99e-16, followed by Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) at FDR=6.44e-15 and Estrogen biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-193144) at FDR=2.16e-13. The five steroids driving these hits are dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estrone (KEGG:C00468), and 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis recovered the same biological module with a perfect 11/11 overlap on the Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) network node at p=0.00042, confirming that all six input steroids cluster within this pathway. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently validated the same pathway (KEGG:map00150) at p=8.391e-06, with the identical five steroids as the RaMP result. The remaining two input compounds, (S)-3-hydroxyisobutyric acid (KEGG:C06001) and indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637), appear in separate peripheral pathways (valine/leucine degradation and tryptophan metabolism respectively) and did not co-enrich with the steroid cluster in any paradigm. Menadione (KEGG:C05377) was not assigned to any significant pathway.

payload_summary.fallback_suggested: use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
